## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kaṇḍakavimānavatthu* (Vv 81) is a canonical poem in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text relates the afterlife of Kanthaka (Pali: Kaṇḍaka), the royal horse who carried Prince Siddhārtha on the night of his departure into homelessness during the Great Renunciation [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship on the life of the Buddha, the text is referenced in the context of the renunciation narrative and early biographical traditions [Nakamura 2000]. Five modern translations across five languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

In the Pali tradition, the verses of the text are cited almost entirely within the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, where 47 shared segments span §1.1–20.2 [DharmaNexus]. It also shares formulaic celestial descriptions with another poem in the same collection, the *Suvaṇṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 78, particularly §12.1–15.3) [DharmaNexus]. While SuttaCentral records no curated parallels in other languages [SuttaCentral], automated text alignments generated by DharmaNexus indicate textual reuse with several Tibetan translations of Buddhist sūtras, including the *Pitāputrasamāgamasūtra* (D0060), the *Saptatathāgatapūrvapraṇidhānaviśeṣavistarasūtra* (D0503), the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra* (D0120), and the *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthānasūtra* (D0287-2) [DharmaNexus].
